brief: GS splits Brazil's FX reaction into an already-realized ~10% initial move and a second leg gated on fiscal delivery (cabinet picks, reform signals), with reversal risk if fiscal measures aren't delivered; unlike 2018, when a divided Congress capped BRL's rally despite a similar first-round-to-result move, Flavio's governability looks better this time, though fiscal pressure is greater now. DI rates closed ~125bps tighter, long-end FRAs near 12.50%, and breaking the 11.5-12% region needs both a Flavio win and a credible fiscal/transition bill; long-end flows were net receiving with only small profit-taking. On equities, GS sees EWZ trading 45-50 near-term with upside room, citing unprecedented Congress/Senate/Executive alignment, while GS's economist expects a gradual multi-year fiscal adjustment rather than a front-loaded one, and the rates desk says a durable equity rally still needs external-market relief. Separately, Tony Pasquariello stays bullish on the S&P into December 31 despite a choppy Q4, arguing higher rates are a headwind, not a wrecking ball, since earnings offset P/E compression from 23x to 19x, and pairs long risk with a short in US Fixed Income even as the Fed delivers one more hike this year and two next year.
